headline: Telling almost-solvable puzzles from hopeless ones can be impossibly hard.
scope: The proof covers the edge-value form with fixed errors; the alphabet is fixed after the errors.
plain: A unique game is a matching puzzle (every answer forces exactly one reply at the other end). In 2002, Subhash Khot conjectured that telling nearly solvable instances from nearly worthless ones stays hard for computers. This paper claims to prove the conjecture by translating logic puzzles into matching puzzles. Companion papers then establish the best possible ratios for Max-Cut, Vertex Cover, Min-UnCut and directed feedback.
doesNot: This does not give a fast algorithm for any of these problems.
origin: This result comes from an unreleased OpenAI model, published in the openai/math release on 6 October 2026.

scorecard.firstStepBy: Subhash Khot, the Unique Games Conjecture
scorecard.significanceWhy: If the proofs hold, they close the central open problem of approximation hardness.

sections.title: The story
sections.body: In 2002, Subhash Khot conjectured that matching puzzles stay hard to approximate even when almost solvable. In 1995, Michel Goemans and David Williamson gave a celebrated cutting algorithm whose ratio became the target to beat. In 2007, Khot and coauthors showed that beating it would refute the conjecture. In 2008, Prasad Raghavendra extended the pattern: the conjecture would fix the best ratio for every constraint problem. These papers prove the conjecture by translating logic puzzles into matching puzzles with no good approximation.

sections.title: Why it matters
sections.body: Settling the conjecture turns dozens of conditional hardness results into unconditional ones. In this language, completeness is the nearly solvable side and soundness is the nearly worthless side. The companion papers do this directly for Max-Cut, Vertex Cover, Min-UnCut and directed feedback.

sections.title: Where it leads
sections.body: The same framework now applies to every fixed constraint language via the basic semidefinite threshold (the limit of a standard equation-solving method). The proofs also separate deterministic from randomized guarantees, claiming nothing about the latter.

sections.title: What it says about AI
sections.body: The manuscripts list OpenAI as author, and the repository states that an internal model produced them. The published reasoning summary shows the model moving from failed gadget ideas to a rank-one noise construction. The Lean catalogue lists formalizations of the Unique Games gap and all four hardness consequences.

hypeCheck: Formally listed but unreviewed: Lean records the reductions without certifying compilation, and specialists have not weighed in.

claims.text: For fixed errors there is a polynomial-time reduction from 3SAT to unique games separating value 1-eps from delta.
claims.sourceLine: For every fixed eps,delta in (0,1/2), there are s>=1 and a deterministic polynomial-time reduction from 3SAT to explicit unweighted Unique Games instances with val >= 1-eps on satisfiable and <= delta on unsatisfiable inputs.

claims.text: This resolves the Unique Games Conjecture in its usual edge-value formulation.
claims.sourceLine: Thus the result resolves the Unique Games Conjecture positively in its usual edge-value formulation [Conjecture 2.5][Khot10].
Khot introduced the Unique Games Conjecture in 2002 and gave an algorithm based on semidefinite rounding [Khot02].

claims.text: Goemans and Williamson gave the celebrated cutting algorithm; Khot et al. tied beating it to the conjecture.
claims.sourceLine: Theorem supplies the Unique Games hypothesis in earlier hardness reductions for cut, covering, constraint-satisfaction problems [KKMO07, KhotRegev2008, Raghavendra08].
